speaker: Speckle-neck
title: The danger of blind greed
text: All out of longing for a golden bangle, the Tiger, in the mud, the man did mangle. Good things come not out of bad things; wisely leave a longed-for ill. Nectar being mixed with poison serves no purpose but to kill. But all gain is got by risk, so I will see into it at least. Trust not water, trust not weapons; trust not clawed nor horned things; neither give thy soul to women, nor thy life to Sons of Kings.
modern_interpretation: Beware of tempting opportunities that promise great rewards but conceal significant dangers. Pursuing something alluring but fundamentally flawed or unethical will inevitably lead to negative consequences, much like poisoned nectar. While risk is inherent in seeking advancement or gain, exercise extreme caution and discernment. Do not place your trust or invest your deepest self in inherently unstable, predatory, or potentially manipulative situations, relationships, or power dynamics.
summary: This wisdom warns against the perilous nature of blind greed and the pursuit of gains through risky, ill-conceived means, stating that bad origins cannot yield good outcomes. It advises extreme caution with unreliable entities and potentially compromising relationships, despite the inherent risks in seeking reward.
actionable_advice: Before committing to any opportunity or relationship that feels too good to be true, pause to critically analyze all potential hidden risks, long-term consequences, and the character of those involved.
embedding_ready_text: The Hitopadesa, in its warning about blind greed, illustrates with the tragic tale of a man mangled for a golden bangle. This wisdom emphasizes that positive outcomes cannot arise from negative or compromised means ('Good things come not out of bad things; wisely leave a longed-for ill. Nectar being mixed with poison serves no purpose but to kill.'). While acknowledging that 'all gain is got by risk,' the text simultaneously urges extreme caution and discernment, advising against placing trust in inherently unstable or dangerous elements like water, weapons, predators, or potentially exploitative relationships ('Trust not water, trust not weapons; trust not clawed nor horned things; neither give thy soul to women, nor thy life to Sons of Kings.'). This teaching guides individuals in emotional regulation around desire and risk, encouraging strategic thinking, discipline, and the courage to avoid situations driven by unchecked greed or naive trust, thereby preventing severe disappointment, harm, and regret in various life domains.
